perspective:
From Ethan Mohamud’s perspective, he has access to:

- He is Ethan Mohamud, a Black man and plumber, close friends with Gary Guo since middle school. Gary is a doctor, and they rely on each other for support.
- He notices Gary working excessive hours at the hospital, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep. Concerned, he invites Gary to a two-day weekend retreat to relax and gain perspective.
- He hears Gary decline, saying he appreciates the concern but cannot because there is too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, he observes Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. He suspects something more than professional obligations is going on.
- He confronts Gary, reminding him they have been friends since middle school, that Gary can tell him anything, and that he is there to help, not judge.
- He hears Gary say it is complicated and that he did not want to burden him. Gary then opens up about pressures managing a new department and personal challenges.
- He offers to help Gary find better balance by prioritizing tasks and delegating responsibilities. Gary agrees and says he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checks in, discusses Gary’s progress and challenges, sees Gary making efforts to change, and offers encouragement. Gary tells him things are better, he is less overwhelmed, and he had time for a movie.
- After a year, Ethan sees Gary managing on his own. He decides to step back, tells Gary he is always a call away and knows Gary has got this. Gary thanks him, says he could not have done it without his support, and feels more in control.
